loop_primitives.evidence: "call the model, stream the answer into the transcript 5: if the model asks for a tool then 6: route the call, append the result to the transcript" (paper Sec. 3.6 Algorithm 1)

multi_agent_topology.evidence: "A harness runs the loop of input synthesis, model calls, and output settlement over one session" (paper Sec. 3.6)

short_term_state.evidence: "Messages shown to the model are a projec-tion over the transcript" (paper Sec. 3.3)

state_persistence.evidence: "a new process of the same id imports the transcript, rebuilds the projection, and continues the session, a cold switch." (paper Sec. 3.8)

rollback.evidence: "Recovery has no rollback and no fork, the rebuilt view equals the view the failed process held" (paper Sec. 3.8)
rollback.note: This covers session recovery only. Component mounts carry tracked inverses (reversible assembly), but these are not a revert of file changes.

timeouts.note: The 5 s write timeout is bus-level (it disconnects the peer), not a timeout on tool calls.

system_prompt_style.evidence: "constructs a bounded contractci+1 specifying the immediate goal, acceptance criteria, boundary constraints, and the task-state records and prior audit reports relevant to execution and verification." (paper Sec. 2.2)
system_prompt_style.note: Per-round prompts assembled from task state, contract and audit reports; prompt-building code not in bundle.

env_context_strategy.evidence: "The backend retains its native planning and tool-use loop and may normally invoke the shell, edit files, write code, run tests, or interact with applications" (paper Sec. 2.3)

context_compaction.evidence: "the executor's interaction history is discarded after each round so that only compact, verified task state persists across the task." (paper Sec. 1)
context_compaction.note: Backend-internal compaction (Claude Code/Codex) not coded.

observation_format.note: Observations are produced by wrapped backends and MCP computer-use plugins; harness conversion code not in bundle.

tool_call_format.note: Tool calling delegated to backend agents (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, dsh); no parser in bundle.

tool_count.note: Tools are those of the wrapped backend; not declared in harness evidence.

edit_primitive.note: Editing done by backend agents.

protocol_standardization.evidence: "Any MCP server can be passed to the agents, not just computer-use ones." (README.md)

loop_primitives.evidence: "Plan → act → verify → checkpoint or recover → repeat — until the work is actually done." (README.md)
loop_primitives.note: Manage-Execute-Audit loop; react inside backends.

planning_granularity.evidence: "The task state is a structured collection of task-relevant records: arequirementrepresents an objective or constraint derived from the original task" (paper Sec. 2.2)

multi_agent_topology.evidence: "| 🧭 **State and next step** | **Manager** | Rebuilds each round from the original goal, verified progress, failure evidence, and remaining work |" (README.md)
multi_agent_topology.note: Manager, GUI/CLI executors and auditors; README says roles are implementation boundaries.

delegation_mechanism.evidence: "Each executor invocation runs as a fresh, budget-bounded episode containing only the information supplied for the current round." (paper Sec. 2.3)

human_in_loop.evidence: "Start a task, choose a backend and model per role, answer approvals, send an instruction mid-run, and stop or restart a run." (README.md)
human_in_loop.note: Manager 'ask' route; human-review gate after repeated timeouts.

short_term_state.evidence: "Each record is marked ascompleted,pending,blocked, oruntrusted, and retains references to the audit evidence supporting its current status." (paper Sec. 2.2)

long_term_memory.note: No cross-run memory surface in bundle; follow-ups continue same run.

state_persistence.evidence: "a follow-up continues the same run from the rounds it already completed." (README.md)

self_verification.evidence: "a read-only auditor to verify the resulting environment state before the next round." (paper Abstract)

retry_policy.evidence: "The loop ends when the audited state satisfies the original task, no permitted subtask can advance the remaining requirements, user input is required, or the round budget is exhausted." (paper Sec. 2.1)
retry_policy.note: Capped by max_rounds 30.

termination_condition.evidence: "| `max_rounds` | `30` | Upper bound on Manage-Execute-Audit rounds before the run stops. |" (README.md)
